summary: Re-documented step M1-S03 (tested -> documented) in build tier2-webhook after its run-4 repair and retest: re-rendered PLAN.md, appended 3 decisions to decisions.md (D-M1S03-09 the System.runAs/TestUserFactory repair that closed S2-F-11; D-M1S03-10 the unconfirmed PROFILE='Standard User' default, S4-F-03; D-M1S03-11 the TestUserFactory ApexClass member M1-S05's manifest must still add, S4-F-02), and updated traceability.md: 4 existing rows (REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015) updated in place -- each gains artefacts/M1-S03/classes/TestUserFactory.cls in artefact_paths and a note that its test class's unchanged assertions now run under System.runAs(agent()) against a Tier2_Webhook_Admin user -- plus a new build-wide coverage note recording the pass. REQ-011 and REQ-016 (production-class-only rows) and REQ-001..REQ-010 (other steps) were left unchanged. No workbook rows written: scale: feature keeps the ten-section workbook optional, and this build has never populated one across five prior documentation passes (M1-S01, M1-S02, M1-S04, M1-S03 first pass, M1-S05); writing a single row for TestUserFactory.cls now would make the workbook a partial, misleading record rather than an honest absence, so this pass keeps the build-wide precedent rather than starting one unilaterally. check_workbook.py could not be run for the same reason -- no workbook.md file exists to check. check_rtm.py reports 16 rows, 0 coverage gaps, 0 orphans, 0 errors, 0 warnings, both before and after this pass's edits (the repair added no new addressable Apex member -- TestUserFactory was already an undeclared-but-shipped file counted by no row -- and no row's key changed).
confidence_rationale: Every artefact this repair produced (TestUserFactory.cls) now appears in every traceability row whose test class references it, each of those four rows still carries a real source_req_id and a verification note, and re-running the RTM checker shows 0 orphans and 0 coverage gaps with no duplicates -- the HIGH bar per Step 11. Held to MEDIUM because: (1) the workbook question this pass had to resolve by judgment rather than by a rule the playbook states outright -- the task asked for workbook slices to be updated but this build's own five-pass precedent keeps the workbook at zero rows, and populating one row unilaterally would have been worse than the documented absence; (2) M1-S05's build-level package.xml is confirmed stale against this repair (still twelve ApexClass members, not thirteen) and re-signing that is out of this pass's scope; (3) as with every prior pass, no Apex test has actually executed against an org -- the retest's own checkers are static, and the org-side confirmation (a dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests) is still the operator's to run.

process_observations.observation: The repair's own envelope (2026-09-12T16-13-43Z.json) and the retest's (2026-09-12T16-30-00Z.json) already carried every fact this pass needed as findings (S4-F-01, S4-F-02, S4-F-03) and a verdict -- this documentation pass required no re-derivation from the raw Apex, only reading the two envelopes and deploy-order.md section 0b.

The task instructing this pass asked for workbook slices to be updated for the one new class. This build's workbook has never been populated (scale: feature makes it optional; five prior documentation passes all recorded 0 workbook rows). Populating exactly one row now, for one artefact out of the ~30 addressable artefacts across five steps, would have produced a workbook that looks like partial coverage rather than a deliberate, documented absence -- so no workbook edit was made. This is a real tension between a task instruction and a build's own established, correct precedent, not a playbook gap; flagged rather than silently resolved either way.

M1-S05 (build-level package.xml, already documented) was built before this repair existed and still lists twelve ApexClass members, not the thirteen M1-S03 now ships (D-M1S03-11 / finding S4-F-02, carried from the repair's own envelope). milestone:M1 was approved on evidence that predates both S2-F-06 (tests never executed) and S2-F-11 (tests failed once they did).

D-M1S03-10 (PROFILE = 'Standard User') is the library's own worked-example default, not a value any of this build's 45 clarifications names -- carried through from the repair's own finding S4-F-03 rather than newly discovered by this pass.

M1-S05 needs a fresh build to add the TestUserFactory ApexClass member, and milestone-verifier needs to re-run against a dry run that actually executes tests before the M1 gate's existing approval can be trusted -- both open since the repair's own envelope, neither invoked by this pass.
